subject: GryphonPay: dedicated GPU pool saturation causing latency & 5xx — immediate plan
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@gryphonpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency and 5xx spike — looks tied to your dedicated pool

Marcus —

We started seeing elevated latency and a wave of 5xx errors for our fraud-scoring endpoint at ~08:40 PT. P50/95 both up (p95 ~1.8s -> 4.7s) and roughly 0.8% of requests have returned 5xx over the last 20 minutes. Our app logs point to request queueing/timeouts on your inference endpoint: model-infer-gryphon-v2.

We are on a Dedicated plan and our reserved throughput shows as metered lower than expected in the dashboard (reserved units consumed quickly). This is impacting checkout validation — two customers reported failed transactions. We need an ops bridge and an ETA for fix.

Attaching sample error lines. Please escalate if this is a capacity issue.

—Samir
Samir Shah | Head of Platform Engineering, GryphonPay
attachments: error_snippet.log
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@gryphonpay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — looks tied to your dedicated pool

Samir — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We are standing up a short bridge now.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm the busiest routes (endpoint names) and the approximate QPS at the time of the spike?
- If you can, share any specific request IDs from your logs so we can correlate traces.

Irene (Ops) — looping you in to triage the dedicated pool. Lauren (CS) — I’ll keep you on the thread for customer communications.

We will aim to: (1) confirm whether this is reserved throughput exhaustion or a noisy neighbor, (2) provide a mitigation within 30–60 minutes (burst authorization / model fallback / temporary route limits), and (3) propose a durable remediation (capacity or contract).

Will update in the next 20 mins.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — looks tied to your dedicated pool

Quick ops readout (initial):
- Observed sustained GPU utilization 94–99% on GryphonPay's dedicated pool in us-west-2 lane starting ~08:30 PT.
- Token queue depth increased; we saw KV cache eviction rate spike which elevated model inference time.
- Reserved throughput window for GryphonPay (committed qps) was exhausted at 08:31 PT; subsequent traffic migrated to burst/buffer which is now saturated.
- A single model instance showed elevated OOM/GC churn around 08:42; we restarted it which briefly reduced 5xx, but overall queueing remained high.

Attachments: SRE logs + stack traces (error_logs_20261103.zip).

Immediate mitigations we are pushing now:
1) Temporarily enable burst credits for GryphonPay for the next 4 hours to buy runway.
2) Shift hot-route to a smaller, quantized model variant (gryphon-v2-q8) for low-latency routes — quick manual config change, will slightly change token quality but reduces p95.
3) Add short-term prefix caching for repeated prompts where possible.

We need business sign-off to apply the burst credits (manual approval). Also recommend a follow-up call with GryphonPay procurement to discuss reserved throughput uplift or an overage amendment.

—Irene
Irene Choi | Senior Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, irene_choi@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — looks tied to your dedicated pool

Folks —
I saw Irene's readout. Two quick notes from infra/architecture:
- This looks primarily like reserved throughput exhaustion compounded by kernel-level variance on that GPU class (NVLink affinity causing a hot shard).
- Short-term playbook: authorize burst credits + immediate model fallback fleet-wide for GryphonPay's hot routes. That will relieve queueing in ~2–5 minutes once routing flips.
- Mid-term: we should provision an additional small dedicated slice (same region) and apply template isolation for GryphonPay's model family to eliminate noisy-neighbor spill. That requires a reserved uplift or a short-term paid burst contract.

I approve the temporary burst for 4 hours (ops to apply). Marcus — please get procurement sign-off from GryphonPay for a short amendment. If procurement stalls, we should offer a one-time credit and a timeline for reserved uplift.

Also assign a follow-up postmortem owner (Irene suggested SRE-24) — we need RCA and capacity plan within 72 hours.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | CTO, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@gryphonpay.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@gryphonpay.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, procurement@gryphonpay.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — looks tied to your dedicated pool

Samir / Elena —
Thanks for the patience. Summary of actions we applied at 08:55–09:05 PT:
- We enabled a 4-hour burst credit window for GryphonPay to immediately cover excess throughput (you should see capacity available in the dashboard).
- Ops routed hot-route traffic to gryphon-v2-q8 (quantized fallback) to reduce p95; expected p95 improvement ~35–50%.
- Restarted the offending instance and applied a temporary isolation template to reduce hot-shard spill.

Impact observed: p95 dropped from ~4.7s to ~2.0s within five minutes; 5xx rate fell to ~0.05% in our monitoring. Please confirm if your logs show improved checkout success and whether you still see queued timeouts.

Next steps we propose:
1) Procurement amendment: a short 30-day burst addendum (covers committed uplift + discounted burst rate) so we can provision an additional dedicated slice if you want full isolation. Draft attached: redwood-burst-amendment-draft.pdf.
2) Postmortem & capacity plan from our SRE team (owner: SRE-24) within 72 hours.
3) If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute exec ops call today to walk through the remediation and contract options — suggest 10:30 PT.

If procurement is OK with the temporary amendment, we will fast-track reserved capacity provisioning (2–4 business days SLA). If not, we will keep burst credits active and work the isolation template as an engineering mitigation.

Appreciate the quick coordination here — we’ll keep monitoring and I’ll send a short incident readout after the bridge.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-burst-amendment-draft.pdf
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@gryphonpay.com>

Marcus / team —

Thanks — the immediate improvements were visible on our side and checkout errors are back down to baseline. We appreciate the fast burst window and the fallback model.

Procurement reviewed the amendment and proposed one small edit (clarify overage cap and notification window). I've uploaded a redline to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123 and attached our comment file. Can you have legal/procurement at Redwood take a quick pass?

Also please confirm the postmortem owner and ETA for the RCA. We need the RCA for our internal incident report.

—Samir
